title: The Microscopic Work of Reading Leadership
author: Coombe, Amy
summary: Amy Coombe argues that effective reading leadership demands microscopic, day-to-day attention to individual student gaps rather than relying on half-termly assessments. Drawing on Direct Instruction and Corrective Reading principles, she explains that every day a student's confusion goes undetected, they practice the error—and with each missed concept, what should feel familiar increasingly feels new. Reading knowledge is compared to a Jenga tower: each piece depends on the one before, and guessing behaviors that go unchallenged in early years arrive entrenched in secondary school. Coombe identifies three traps reading leaders fall into—waiting for periodic tests, accepting some gaps as inevitable, and attributing failure to the child rather than to instruction. The prescription is relentless, data-informed coaching conversations organized around dozens of granular questions about signal clarity, student tracking, error correction, and fluency checkout fidelity, every single week.
points: Every day a reading confusion goes undetected, the student is practicing the wrong behavior—making swift identification and immediate correction the first principle of reading leadership.

The Direct Instruction principle that 100% of students can learn all content eliminates the excuse that some knowledge gaps are inevitable; every missing piece must be addressed before the next lesson builds on it.
When students miss foundational content, the 10–15% of genuinely new material per lesson effectively becomes 20–30%, eventually making the programme incoherent for those students.
Reading leaders must stop attributing failure to a child's attention, diagnosis, or fit with the programme, and instead identify precisely what changes in instruction can close the gap.

Weekly coaching conversations should be structured around dozens of granular questions—signal clarity, finger tracking, error revision, fluency checkout accuracy—not broad impressionistic walk-throughs.
